name: Rulemaking timing

subjectOf.text: A core tenet of incomplete contract theory, that rulemakers should act only when sufficient information becomes available, is often politically, economically, and practically undesirable or impossible.
subjectOf.abstract: a core tenet of incomplete contract theory – rulemakers should act when sufficient information becomes available – is often political- ly, economically, and practically undesirable or impossible
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Dynamic Regulation via Governmental Contracts (2014)

subjectOf.text: Because rulemaking is subject to regulatory cycles and to a classic collective action problem, rules are generally not enacted at the moment appropriate information for rulemaking becomes available.
